Subject: Evidence request: CI code-signing + pipeline guardrails

Hi Marissa,

We are preparing our SIG/SOC2 intake for Finova and need artifacts that demonstrate how you handle code signing, short-lived key usage, and pipeline gating for production releases. Specifically can you provide: 

- A concise description of the code-signing workflow (who signs, where keys are stored, rotation cadence).
- Evidence (logs or sample CI outputs) showing a successful signing step in the pipeline.
- CI/CD gating configuration or policies (e.g., OPA checks, automated tests, manual approvals).
- How you protect secrets used in signing (KMS, HSM, Vault), and proof of limited lifespan for signing credentials.
- Any runbook or change-management record for emergency release exceptions.

If possible, please attach representative artifacts (redacted logs are fine) and give a timeline when we can review them with your team. We are trying to close this by end of quarter.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Park
Security Engineer, Finova Payments
elena@finova.com

Subject: Re: Evidence request: CI code-signing + pipeline guardrails

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. We can provide a concise package and a short walkthrough. Plan below and attachments in this thread: signing-policy.pdf (policy summary), pipeline-diagram.png (stage layout), and a redacted ci-job-output.log showing the signing step.

Quick answers up front:
- We use cosign for binary and container signing. Keys are provisioned from an HSM-backed KMS and surfaced to ephemeral signing agents via Vault dynamic credentials.
- Signing occurs in a dedicated signing job in our release pipeline after all gating checks pass. Keys are never stored in plaintext in the repo or build images.
- Rotation: KMS-managed keys rotate yearly; Vault ephemeral signing tokens are time-limited (default 15 minutes).
- Gating: unit + integration + security scans must pass; OPA policy policies enforce commit provenance and required approvals. Manual approval step before prod promotion for services with critical PCI/PHI scopes.

Next steps: Irene will drop the runbook snippet and a sample OPA policy. Karthik will attach a sanitized CI log with timestamps. Can you confirm whether you need raw logs or a PDF bundle? We can do a quick 30-min call this afternoon if you prefer to walk through live.

Best,

Elena — adding details on implementation and the runbook excerpt you asked for.

On our side the signing pipeline looks like this (high level):
- Build stage produces artifacts (containers, wheels).
- Policy check stage (OPA + SAST) validates provenance and policy assertions.
- Signing stage runs on a paused ephemeral runner in a hardened subnet with no external egress. The runner requests a one-time signing token from Vault. Vault uses an HSM-backed KMS to mint a short-lived signing credential (cosign key material wrapped and never persisted).
- Signed artifact is pushed to our registry with a provenance envelope. The pipeline writes an immutable record to our audit log (append-only storage with retention tied to customer SLAs).

Runbook excerpt (redacted):
- Condition: failed signing due to KMS timeout or rotated key mismatch.
- Action: abort promotion -> notify on-call infra -> escalate to security and release manager.
- Emergency release path: allowed only with two manager approvals + CT audit capture; changes recorded in Jira ticket and signed release bundle attached.

Where we store artifacts/logs: central log store (w/ retention policy), and a signed manifest is uploaded to the customer evidence Drive folder (link provided).

I attached the signing-policy.pdf that summarizes the HSM/KMS and Vault flows. Karthik will post the sanitized log next. Happy to jump on a call to show the vault-to-runner handshake if helpful.

Irene

- 2024-05-28T18:12:32Z | OPA policy: PASS (commit provenance check)
- 2024-05-28T18:13:05Z | Vault request: /v1/secret/signing-token -> 200 OK (token ttl 900s)
- 2024-05-28T18:13:18Z | cosign sign -> SHA256:abcd...
- 2024-05-28T18:13:25Z | Upload manifest -> registry.prod.redwood/servicex@sha256:...

Notes: the log is redacted to remove environment-specific hostnames and IPs. The pipeline job name is release/sign-and-publish:v1.2.3. We also include an OPA policy snippet in the Drive link that enforces required approvals for prod promotion.

If you want raw system-level logs for the signing host we can provide those under an NDA; otherwise the sanitized bundle should be sufficient for SIG/SOC2 review.
